metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code (VB6) present with a deployable entry point (Form_Load). Single-service desktop application with persistent data store.
metadata.archetype_justification: Has persistent state (Microsoft Access .mdb database), CRUD operations (INSERT INTO Customers), and user-specific data.

tech_stack.architecture: Desktop client with direct database access (Microsoft Access .mdb on SMB file share)

findings.title: No API Interface — Direct Database Access Required
findings.description: The application is a Win32 desktop EXE (VB6) that connects directly to a Microsoft Access .mdb file on an SMB network share. There is no REST, GraphQL, AsyncAPI, or any programmatic interface. Integration requires direct database access or UI automation.
findings.gap: No API exists. The only integration path is direct Access database manipulation via OLEDB/ODBC or RPA against the desktop UI.
findings.recommendation: Design and implement a REST API layer that exposes customer CRUD operations, wrapping the existing database. Migrate from Access .mdb to a supported database.

findings.title: No Idempotency on Write Operations
findings.description: The INSERT operation has no idempotency controls. No idempotency key, no unique constraint enforcement, no deduplication logic. Repeated submissions create duplicate records.
findings.gap: No idempotency mechanism exists. Agent retries would create duplicate customer records.
findings.recommendation: Implement idempotency key support in write endpoints. Add unique business key constraints.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND no idempotency controls on INSERT operations.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: Agent retries and LLM non-determinism would create duplicate customer records without idempotency controls.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Add unique business key constraint on Customers table
blocker_remediation.target_state: All write endpoints accept idempotency key header

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: Single hardcoded database password shared by all users. No service accounts, OAuth2 client credentials, API keys, mTLS, or any machine identity authentication.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication exists. An agent cannot be uniquely identified or attributed.
findings.recommendation: Implement centralized identity provider (Cognito, Okta) with OAuth2 client credentials flow for machine-to-machine authentication.

findings.title: No Audit Logging
findings.description: Zero logging of any kind. No audit trail for any operation. On Error Resume Next silently swallows all errors without recording them.
findings.gap: No audit logging, no immutable storage, no principal attribution in logs.
findings.recommendation: Implement CloudTrail and application-level structured audit logging with immutable storage (S3 Object Lock).

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND zero audit logging exists.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: Write-enabled agents require immutable audit trails for compliance (EU AI Act, SOX). No logging of any kind exists.

findings.title: No Compensation or Rollback Capability
findings.description: No transaction management, no saga pattern, no compensation logic, no undo capability. Database corrupts monthly from concurrent access.
findings.gap: No rollback or compensation mechanism. Failed agent workflows leave database in partial/corrupt state.
findings.recommendation: Implement database transactions with commit/rollback semantics. Design compensation endpoints for multi-step workflows.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND no transaction/compensation logic exists.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: Agent-initiated multi-step write workflows cannot be rolled back. Access database corruption is already occurring monthly.

findings.title: Unscoped Sensitive Data Access
findings.description: System stores customer PII. The only integration path (direct database access) exposes ALL fields in ALL tables without filtering. Single shared password provides full access to everything.
findings.gap: B1: No mechanism to scope agent data access — direct DB access exposes all fields. B2: Single shared password with no role differentiation.
findings.recommendation: Implement API layer with field-level scoping and access control differentiation. Separate DTOs for agent-facing responses.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND B1 fired (unscoped data access via direct DB).
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: Direct database access provides unrestricted access to all customer PII. No API layer exists to filter sensitive fields.

b1.reasoning: Only integration path is direct DB access which exposes all fields without scoping. agent_scope=write-enabled.

b2.reasoning: Single shared password (crm2005pw) gives identical full access to all callers. No role differentiation.

b3.reasoning: No data classification metadata, tags, or field-level sensitivity annotations exist.

findings.title: No Data Residency Controls
findings.description: Customer data resides on SMB file share with no residency controls, no region configuration, no data sovereignty policies. No restrictions on data transmission.
findings.gap: No data residency policies, no region controls, no egress restrictions.
findings.recommendation: Document data residency requirements. Implement region-locked storage with egress controls when migrating to cloud.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND no data residency controls exist for customer PII.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: Write-enabled agent could transmit customer data across compliance boundaries. No guardrails exist.

findings.title: No Scoped Permissions
findings.description: Single shared database password provides full access. No concept of scoped permissions — every user and potential agent gets identical full-access credentials.
findings.gap: No authorization model exists. Cannot grant agent read-only access or restrict by resource type.
findings.recommendation: Implement RBAC with scoped IAM policies in replacement API layer. Define per-agent permission sets.

findings.title: No Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization exists. INSERT operations execute without any permission check. No mechanism to allow read but prevent write/delete.
findings.gap: No ABAC, RBAC, or permission matrix. All callers can perform all operations.
findings.recommendation: Design fine-grained permission model (read/write/delete per resource type) in replacement API.

findings.title: No Identity Propagation
findings.description: No identity propagation mechanism. Environ("USERNAME") is a local environment variable read, not a delegation framework. No JWT, OAuth token exchange, or on-behalf-of flow.
findings.gap: Cannot distinguish agent-as-self vs agent-on-behalf-of-user. No token exchange pattern.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2 on-behalf-of flow with distinct auth flows for service-to-service vs user-delegated calls.

findings.title: Hardcoded Credentials in Source Code
findings.description: Database password 'crm2005pw' hardcoded as a constant in VB6 source. No secrets management, no rotation, visible to anyone with source access.
findings.gap: Credentials embedded in source code with no rotation, no secrets manager, no environment-variable abstraction.
findings.recommendation: Migrate credentials to AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation. Remove hardcoded credentials from source.

findings.title: No Concurrency Controls
findings.description: No concurrency controls exist. README confirms monthly corruption from concurrent writes. On Error Resume Next suppresses locking errors.
findings.gap: No optimistic locking, no version fields, no ETags, no conditional writes.
findings.recommendation: Implement optimistic locking with version fields when migrating to proper database.

findings.title: No Transaction Limits or Blast Radius Controls
findings.description: No transaction limits exist. No mechanism to limit records an agent could modify, no spend caps, no bulk operation size limits.
findings.gap: No per-caller business transaction limits. No bulk operation caps.
findings.recommendation: Implement configurable transaction limits (max records per session, max operations per hour) in replacement API.

findings.title: No PII Redaction Framework
findings.description: No logging framework and no PII redaction controls. System handles customer PII without any redaction, masking, or structured logging with field filtering.
findings.gap: No PII masking, no log scrubbing, no structured logging framework.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured logging with PII masking middleware from day one in replacement service.

findings.title: No Draft/Pending State
findings.description: No concept of draft or pending state. INSERT commits immediately with no intermediate reviewable state.
findings.gap: No draft/pending status fields, no approval workflow, no two-step commit.
findings.recommendation: Design status-based workflow (DRAFT → PENDING_REVIEW → COMMITTED) in replacement data model.

findings.title: No Configurable Approval Gates
findings.description: No approval mechanism exists. All operations execute immediately without any configurable approval step.
findings.gap: No approval API, no status-based workflows requiring confirmation.
findings.recommendation: Implement approval gates in replacement API layer with configurable operation-level flags.

findings.title: No Queryable State API
findings.description: No API to expose current state. Database contains records but no endpoints for agents to inspect state before taking action.
findings.gap: No GET endpoints, no status query APIs. State accessible only via direct SQL.
findings.recommendation: Implement GET endpoints for resource state in replacement API layer.

findings.title: SQL Injection — No Input Validation
findings.description: Zero input validation. User input concatenated directly into SQL strings creating SQL injection vulnerability. Malformed agent input would corrupt data or crash queries.
findings.gap: No validation library, no parameterized queries, no schema enforcement, no structured validation errors.
findings.recommendation: Implement parameterized queries (minimum) and request validation middleware with structured error responses.

findings.title: Local Timestamps Without UTC Normalization
findings.description: CreatedOn uses VBA Now() (local machine time). No timezone normalization, no updated_at field, no freshness signaling.
findings.gap: No UTC normalization, no update timestamps, no freshness headers.
findings.recommendation: Implement UTC-based created_at/updated_at timestamps and freshness headers in replacement.

findings.title: No Schema Versioning or API Contracts
findings.description: No schema documentation, versioning, or API contracts. Database schema is implicit from INSERT statement only. No migration files, no changelog.
findings.gap: No versioned schema, no API contract, no breaking change detection.
findings.recommendation: Define formal database schema with migration files. Implement OpenAPI spec with versioning.

findings.title: Zero Test Coverage
findings.description: No tests of any kind. No unit tests, integration tests, API tests, or CI pipeline. Compiled on one developer's machine.
findings.gap: Zero automated test coverage.
findings.recommendation: Implement comprehensive API test suites with CI pipeline in replacement service.

findings.title: No Encryption at Rest
findings.description: Access .mdb 'password' is trivially crackable. No real encryption at rest — no KMS, no disk encryption.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest. Data effectively unencrypted on SMB file share.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to cloud database with KMS customer-managed key encryption at rest.

findings.title: No Sandbox or Staging Environment
findings.description: No non-production environment. Only production with manual EXE distribution. No Docker-compose, no seed data, no environment-specific config.
findings.gap: No staging or sandbox for testing agent behavior without risk to live data.
findings.recommendation: Provision staging environment with synthetic data when building replacement service.

findings.title: No Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No HTTP/RPC surface — machine-readable spec is not applicable to current desktop architecture.
findings.gap: No OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL schema, or equivalent specification.
findings.recommendation: Generate OpenAPI spec from annotations when implementing replacement REST API.

findings.title: No Structured Error Responses
findings.description: No HTTP/RPC surface — structured error responses not applicable. Current error handling is On Error Resume Next with MsgBox.
findings.gap: No structured error format for machine consumption.
findings.recommendation: Design structured JSON error format with error code, message, and retryable flag for replacement API.

findings.title: No Event Emission for State Changes
findings.description: No event emission capability. Direct database writes with no notification mechanism. Nightly DTS/SSIS sync is batch, not real-time.
findings.gap: No webhooks, events, CDC pipeline, or message queue integration.
findings.recommendation: Implement DynamoDB Streams or EventBridge events for state changes in replacement architecture.

findings.title: No Agent Identity Suspension Capability
findings.description: No authentication surface — system has no concept of agent identities to suspend. Single shared password cannot be revoked per-agent.
findings.gap: No per-agent identity lifecycle (create, suspend, revoke).
findings.recommendation: Implement per-agent API keys or Cognito app clients with individual revocation in replacement system.

findings.title: No Rate Limiting (No HTTP Surface)
findings.description: No HTTP/RPC surface — API-layer rate limiting is not applicable. Only natural throughput limitation from Access database file locking.
findings.gap: No rate limiting mechanism at any layer.
findings.recommendation: Implement API Gateway usage plans with per-agent throttling in replacement service.

findings.title: No Data Quality Monitoring
findings.description: No data quality metrics, profiling, or completeness monitoring. Monthly database corruption noted but unmonitored.
findings.gap: No quality dashboards, profiling, or freshness SLAs.
findings.recommendation: Implement data quality profiling and monitoring during migration.

findings.title: No Data Catalog or Metadata Layer
findings.description: No data catalog, metadata layer, or data dictionary. Database schema undocumented — field meanings inferred from column names only.
findings.gap: No documented data semantics beyond column names in INSERT statement.
findings.recommendation: Document database schema with business semantics during migration planning.

findings.title: No Tracing or Structured Logging
findings.description: No HTTP/RPC surface and no agent-initiated request path. Desktop client with no logging, no tracing, no correlation IDs.
findings.gap: No tracing, no structured logging, no correlation IDs.
findings.recommendation: Implement OpenTelemetry and structured JSON logging in replacement API.

findings.title: No Alerting Configuration
findings.description: No HTTP/RPC surface — alerting on API error rates not applicable. No monitoring or alerting of any kind.
findings.gap: No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, no alerting.
findings.recommendation: Configure CloudWatch alarms with anomaly detection for replacement API.

findings.title: No Infrastructure as Code
findings.description: No HTTP/RPC surface and no auth surface — infrastructure governance not applicable for current desktop architecture. No IaC exists.
findings.gap: No Terraform, CDK, or CloudFormation. Manually managed Windows file server.
findings.recommendation: Implement IaC for all infrastructure when building replacement service.

findings.title: No CI/CD Pipeline
findings.description: No HTTP/RPC surface — API contract testing not applicable. No CI/CD pipeline exists. Compiled on one developer's machine.
findings.gap: No CI/CD, no automated builds, no contract testing.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD with contract testing for replacement API.

findings.title: No Rollback Capability
findings.description: No deployed HTTP/RPC surface — rollback not applicable. Manual EXE distribution with no versioning or rollback.
findings.gap: No deployment automation, no rollback mechanism.
findings.recommendation: Implement blue/green deployments with automatic rollback for replacement.

evaluations.title: Structured Response Format
evaluations.reason: No API/serialization surface exists — informational signal, no finding emitted.

evaluations.title: Asynchronous Operation Support
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no evidence of operations >30s or long-running workflows within this application.

evaluations.title: Rate Limit Documentation and Headers
evaluations.reason: No API/HTTP surface exists — informational signal, no finding emitted.

evaluations.title: Circuit Breakers and Resilience
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no evidence of calling other services or external APIs.

evaluations.title: Graceful Degradation Signaling
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no priority provided and not on documented critical path.

evaluations.title: Selective Query Support
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no list/query endpoints with potentially unbounded results (no API surface).

evaluations.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
evaluations.reason: Field names (Customers, Name, CreatedBy, CreatedOn) are human-readable and semantically meaningful. No legacy abbreviations requiring lookup.

evaluations.title: Business Outcome Metrics
evaluations.reason: No metrics or telemetry surface of any kind — informational signal, no finding emitted.

items.summary: Resolve all 7 BLOCKERs and critical RISK-SAFETY findings. Build API layer, implement machine identity, audit logging, compensation logic, and data scoping. Address hardcoded credentials and concurrency controls.
Address remaining RISK-SAFETY and RISK-QUALITY findings. Implement identity propagation, transaction limits, input validation, schema versioning, encryption, staging environment, and observability.
Address remaining quality and informational improvements: test coverage, event emission, data quality monitoring, and data catalog.

recommended_actions.action: Build REST API layer replacing direct database access
recommended_actions.rationale: API-Q1 is the foundational blocker. Every other remediation (auth, audit, scoping) depends on having a programmatic interface to enforce controls against.

recommended_actions.action: Deploy centralized identity provider with machine identity
recommended_actions.rationale: Machine identity is the prerequisite for scoped permissions, action-level auth, and meaningful audit logging.

recommended_actions.action: Migrate from Access .mdb to cloud database with encryption
recommended_actions.rationale: Access .mdb cannot support transactions, concurrency controls, encryption at rest, or region-locked storage. Database migration is a prerequisite for multiple blockers.

recommended_actions.action: Implement audit logging with immutable storage
recommended_actions.rationale: Write-enabled agent operations require immutable audit trails for compliance and forensics.

recommended_actions.action: Remove hardcoded credentials and implement secrets management
recommended_actions.rationale: Hardcoded credentials are immediately exploitable. Rotation via Secrets Manager is a quick win.
